svg.text: Draft. Pairs with managing-experiences.scenarios.md — the ordering, the confirmation and the nine rating values come from it. Settles where experiences live: the restaurant's own screen.
Corner slice, still the best one
Newest first, by the day it happened. Undated experiences come last.
Remove opens the confirmation drawn below.
Click the left half of a star for a half star. Clear leaves it with no rating at all.
Leave empty if you can't remember.
Corner slice, still the best one
At least one of the three. Save stays disabled while all three are empty.
Nine values: 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 3.5, 4, 4.5, 5 — plus no rating, which is not nought.
the default, and not a score of nought
half steps all the way up
One control, nine reachable values, and no way to express 0, 3.7 or 5.5 — the three things
the scenarios reject. A slider or a number field would let the owner type all three.
Confirmed first. The experience is destroyed, not kept.
Queue out the door · no date
Confirmed because it cannot be undone. Taking a restaurant off the list is
confirmed too, but that keeps its experiences — this destroys the note outright.
The dialog names the experience, which is the only way to tell apart several
Fill and outline change together, so these survive greyscale.
